trigger: Any authenticated or guest customer requesting an ACL-restricted entity
exploit_path: AuthorizeAsync returns true whenever the customer has any role at all instead of an allowed role; a Registered customer reaches an Administrators-restricted entity
notes: Role-intersection replaced by a bare has-any-role check; every customer belongs to >=1 role so the ACL is effectively open

trigger: Admin-area request from an IP that shares a prefix with an allowlisted IP
exploit_path: Exact IP match weakened to StartsWith; allowlisting 10.0.0.1 also admits 10.0.0.100 etc., so a same-subnet host reaches the admin area
notes: SecuritySettings.AdminAreaAllowedIpAddresses becomes a loose prefix filter instead of an exact allowlist

trigger: Any request by a customer whose account is flagged MustChangePassword
exploit_path: MustChangePassword clause dropped; an admin-forced password reset is never enforced and the account keeps using the old credential
notes: Only password-expiry still forces the change; the forced-change flag is ignored

trigger: Any request carrying an X-Requested-With header
exploit_path: Client-controlled AJAX exemption short-circuits the forced-MFA redirect; sending X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest lets an account operate without the required second factor
notes: Forced-MFA enforcement bypassable via a spoofable request header

trigger: A Topic/TopicDetails request with any topicId while the store is closed
exploit_path: Topic exemption broadened to all topics; a non-AccessibleWhenStoreClosed topic is served to an anonymous visitor while the store is closed
notes: AccessibleWhenStoreClosed allowlist check removed from the closed-store gate

trigger: Any request under a PunchOut session older than PunchOutSettings.TimeToExpire
exploit_path: Session age/expiry branch removed; a stale PunchOut session is never invalidated and a later actor keeps ordering under the buyer context
notes: Only controller/action restrictions remain; time-based session invalidation is gone

trigger: A Registered (or any non-admin) customer requests an ACL-restricted entity (e.g. a product/category/topic) whose ACL is set to another role
exploit_path: Role-intersection replaced by customerRoleIds.Any() && allowedRoleIds.Any(); both lists are non-empty for a restricted entity so any customer holding at least one role is authorized without actually sharing an allowed role
notes: Entity-ACL AuthorizeAsync(entityTypeName, entityId, customer) no longer verifies the customer belongs to a role granted access to the entity

trigger: Any authenticated or guest customer invokes a permission-gated operation (every customer belongs to >=1 customer role)
exploit_path: Per-role permission lookup replaced by customerRoles.Any(); the named permission (e.g. an admin ManageX permission) is never checked so any customer with a role is authorized

trigger: A customer whose role has no permission records (e.g. a freshly created restricted role) invokes a permission-gated operation
exploit_path: An empty-permissions short-circuit returns true before the SystemName comparison, so a role with no explicit permissions is fail-open authorized for every permission
notes: PermissionService.AuthorizeAsync(permissionRecordSystemName, customerRoleId) treats an unconfigured role as allowed instead of denied
